key_insight: Localized, function-specific subnetworks in an LLM can be selectively updated to enable continual learning with much less forgetting.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a practical path to resource-efficient model adaptation by constraining training and optimizer state updates to the smallest functional region needed for each new task.
method: Use gradient-attribution profiling to identify cognition-associated subnetworks with low overlap.
Route each training example to its matched functional subnetwork for isolated updates.
Restrict both parameter changes and optimizer states via CiMEO (Function-isolated Memory-Efficient Optimization).
evidence_signal: On 1.4 million sequential instructions, CiMEO achieved the best average performance across five benchmarks covering programming, exam-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning, while reducing catastrophic forgetting.
watch_item: Functional routing may be sensitive to how subnetworks are identified and mapped, so misassignment could limit gains or fail to generalize across tasks.
paper_title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
